theses.title: The one-paragraph story
theses.text:
## The one-paragraph story

A predecessor system (not present in this repo) proved the concept and then
collapsed under its own success: roughly 140 accumulated feedback rules loaded
as prose pushed fresh sessions toward 400–500k tokens of always-on context,
where rules fired wrongly or vanished when needed most. In the project's RPG
vocabulary, it brought the **whole stash into every map** — as if a character
carried gear for every damage type when the encounter called only for cold
resistance. In plain language, irrelevant rules consumed attention and created
unintended interactions before the task began. The author's implementation
answers with _compiled_ rules: each correction becomes a typed mechanism (a
permission, a guard, a reactor, an evaluator, a transformer, a workflow gate)
attached only where relevant. A session in that profile gets **a build, not a
biography** — one active behavior, a handful of linked supports, its selected
safety layer, and the exact task state. The platform supplies the compiler and
mechanism contracts without prescribing that loadout. The [starter proof](../evidence/WO-118/README.md) completed resident-owned scratch delivery and review repair with writer replacement and resident restart; a fresh export demonstrated live status, while efficiency remains unmeasured.

theses.title: The core bet
theses.text:
## The core bet

> "The true work of the inventor consists in choosing among these combinations
> so as to eliminate the useless ones... the rules that must guide the choice
> are extremely fine and delicate. It's almost impossible to state them
> precisely; they must be felt rather than formulated." — Poincaré, via Pirsig

Generation is cheap and getting cheaper; the scarce asset is the **selection
function** — the operator's sense of what is good, currently exercised one
correction at a time. DotLn's bet is not that this delicate judgment can be
exhaustively formulated. It is that useful operational approximations can be
progressively arrived at: source incidents preserve what was felt, candidate
mechanisms approach it from different directions, and regression fixtures show
where each construction agrees or diverges. As mathematical or geometric
techniques can converge on a shape without becoming the shape itself, the
formulation is an instrument for approaching the operator's selection function,
not a claim to contain it precisely. **The model changes; the organization
survives.** Claude, Codex, a human, a shell script, and a future model are
interchangeable occupants of the same actor slot.

That bet needs an excellent foundation before it needs a long feature list. In
the reference implementation, the smallest useful loop—declare intent, see what
the system understood, observe authorized progress, receive timely feedback,
and inspect evidence—should already feel responsive, legible, and worth
repeating. Competitive gap-filling does not excuse a weak loop. When another
system introduces a useful idea, DotLn first asks whether the exact behavior can
be accommodated by existing primitives, compositions, ports, and runtime
lowerings. If not, the difference becomes evidence for one missing primitive or
boundary, not permission to bolt on an opaque special case. Integration and
semantic accommodation are preferred to imitation; both preserve every
capability contract the receiving implementation declares and expose any
omitted or lossy capability.

theses.title: The differentiated interface
theses.text:
## The differentiated interface

DotLn's second thesis is about _authoring_, not running:

> "I will take the entire Business, Leadership, and Personal Development shelf
> at Barnes & Noble and just map them to different agent / subagent
> communication structures... at once anyone who has read those books is an
> expert in some feature of the app — and it turns all those books into
> programming books overnight."

The analogies are not documentation — **the analogies are the ways you mix and
match the agents**. Every pattern (5S, the Ladder of Leadership, mitigated
speech, Theory of Constraints, commedia dell'arte roles, the
Algorithms-to-Live-By policies) compiles into exact mechanics, and the same
compiled program renders through an open-ended set of isomorphically equivalent
views: an RPG character with a Path-of-Exile-style socket-and-link build, a
business pattern card, a statechart, a function table, a marble/Morse temporal
track, a TypeScript DSL, an event timeline. Friendly metaphors are authoring
languages, never camouflage: every view either provably compiles to the same
normalized program or is labeled a lossy projection with the exact mechanics one
click away.

### Shape-first synthesis

The operator uses situations and analogies to communicate a desired **shape**: a
relationship, interaction, transition, contrast, feedback loop, or felt quality.
Literal similarity to the reference is not the acceptance test unless a specific
literal detail becomes load-bearing. Preserve the experience first, then
progressively lower it through observable interaction, domain mechanics,
contracts and evidence, and finally technology selected from representative
environment evidence. An imperfect analogy can carry a precise requirement;
source accidents do not become ontology by resemblance.

This is the standing interpretation rule for earlier and future operator
ideation. Its fullest product expression is the first-party application thesis,
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md), but it applies to the whole platform.

theses.title: Three horizons, one kernel
theses.text:
## Three horizons, one kernel

1. **Work operating system** — workstreams, disposable workers, evidence-backed
   completion, offline-capable state, a near-empty main thread. The immediate
   product.
2. **Executable pattern workshop** — the shelf-to-mechanism compiler and the
   drag-a-card-onto-an-agent authoring surface. The differentiated product.
3. **Agent ecology & simulation laboratory** — paired counterfactual runs,
   first-divergence detection, agent swaps, reflection-policy experiments over
   recorded event logs. The research product.

Horizon 3 must emerge from the same kernel (deterministic replay is what makes
counterfactuals possible at all) and is not allowed to distort Horizon 1.
The [workstream application candidate](12-workstream-application.md) develops
Horizon 1 through concrete end-user journeys and gradual workflow replacement,
including one outcome spanning multiple repositories. It leaves deployment and
application identity open and does not allocate another release rung.
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md) is the operator-named application destination that
joins Horizons 2 and 3: prose-authored patterns and ad hoc interventions become
playable inside an inspectable counterfactual community. Naming the destination
does not move it ahead of the release ladder or make its application-local
content kernel doctrine.

theses.title: Mission — increase the chance of operator flow
theses.text:
## Mission — increase the chance of operator flow

This is the mission of the author's personal implementation and a motivating
use of the platform, not a compulsory objective or operating policy for every
DotLn owner.

AI-assisted work commonly falls into a babysitting mode: the operator repeatedly
restates context, supplies procedural guidance, coordinates tools and workers,
checks unsupported completion claims, recovers stalled work, and spends active
attention on the machinery instead of the idea. The desired alternative is not
unbounded improvisation or confidence without evidence. It is a sustained
creative flow in which the operator can keep the idea and implementation
direction in mind while the surrounding work behaves dependably.

The reference implementation's mission is to improve the conditions for that
**operator flow state**.
Supporting research, capability-building, coordination, routine procedure,
recovery, and verification should happen automatically when authorized,
predictably when routine, and helpfully when a genuinely material decision needs
the operator. Product and research investment should favor capabilities that
remove recurring supervision and avoidable context switches without exporting
their cost into correctness, authority, evidence, privacy, or recoverability.

The implementation cannot promise or infer a person's psychological state. It can
reduce interruption, repetition, manual ceremony, and rediscovery; preserve
intent and working context across handoffs; package necessary interruptions as
decision-ready inputs; and make recovery unsurprising. Under its selected
profile, flow does not silently authorize scope expansion, skipped verification,
perpetual action, or self-certification. “Give an agent a build, not your
biography” remains useful architectural shorthand for one mechanism serving
this larger mission.

exclusions.text:
Not an agent, an agent harness, or an agent-orchestration layer, as its
  identity. DotLn is an **agentic platform**: the shared substrate on which
  people and software actors hold work, authority, and evidence. It contains an
  orchestration layer and hosts harnesses as observed environments
  ([runtime primitive catalogs](03-architecture.md#runtime-primitive-catalogs)),
  but neither of those is what it is.
Not a prompt library, and not a wrapper that makes one vendor's model nicer.

Not a prescribed catalog of ideal agents, roles, personalities, workflows, or
  organizational doctrine. Bundled patterns are examples and optional starting
  points, not kernel truth.

Not dependent on a public marketplace. Local files, private catalogs,
  organization-internal registries, and offline or air-gapped installations
  remain complete authoring and distribution paths.

Not one prescribed autonomy curve. Presence and recorded time are policy
  inputs; an explicit owner policy may hold, shrink, grow, peak, reset, or loop
  scope and authority within its declared ceiling.

In the reference implementation, not a metrics theater: no invented numbers,
  no activity-as-progress, evidence precedes "done," and utilization is not the
  objective. A profile that omits verification says so instead.

The reference implementation is not finished when it works for its author:
  v1.0 means a person who has never read these docs can declare a bounded intent
  and receive a verifiable result.

orders.title: WO-230 — A target publish describes the change its pull request shows: the Change table, the base-tree exemption and the no-change check are taken from the merge base of the subject and the target's base branch when the subject has moved past its activation base, the body names the activation base that merge base descends from, and the plan gate's path advisory skips the launchpad's own record paths
orders.objective:
When a registered target order's subject descends from a
base-branch commit later than its activation base, the session publish's
pull request describes the change the forge shows and nothing more, and the
plan gate warns only about paths a publish would meet:

- **The table and its exemptions come from the merge base.** In
  `publishTargetDraft` and `publishTargetWorktree`, the base for
  `targetChanges`, `baseTreePaths` and `composeTargetBody` is the merge
  base of the subject commit (the draft commit; the records commit) and the
  target's base branch as fetched at publish, whenever the activation base is
  an ancestor of that merge base; when the two are equal, every byte of
  today's table, exemptions and body is unchanged. A subject that does not
  descend from the activation base still refuses as today.
- **The no-change checks compare against the described base.** A working
  tree equal to the described base's tree refuses "no change to draft"; a
  records commit equal to it refuses "no target change to publish".
- **The body says which base it describes.** The Change section's closing
  sentence names the described base and, when it differs from the
  activation base, adds "activated at base <activation>, which <described>
  descends from". The activation base stays the base of every record,
  event, registry entry and verification; nothing rebinds it.
- **The fetch comes first and a failed fetch refuses.** The base branch is
  fetched through the lane before the merge base is read, as release close
  fetches it; a fetch failure refuses before any push, naming the remote,
  with the prepared work retained for the retry.
- **The plan gate advises on target paths only.** `targetOrderPathAdvisories`
  skips an Execution-plan path under the order's own record roots
  (`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/`, `docs/verifications/WO-NNN/`,
  `docs/final-reviews/WO-NNN/`, as the launchpad's configured roots
  resolve them), because those files reach a target only as moved kit
  records, which the lint exempts from the identifier rule by design; a
  target-side path carrying an identifier or a review word is advised as
  today.

orders.title: WO-224 — The Entropy Reducer reviews a registered target repository or a workstream's repositories: `npm run entropy -- review --repository <id> [<commit>]` and `--workstream WS-NNN` freeze the registered clone at a recorded commit the way the launchpad is frozen, run the pinned reviewer, the blinded refutation and the immutable receipts in the launchpad, dispose into its register with rows a pass allocates to the workstream's orders, and ship in the kit (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
An operator at a launchpad, core or an exported instance,
runs the Entropy Reducer against a registered target repository or a
workstream's repositories with the discipline the launchpad review has:

- **The subject is a registered repository at a recorded commit.** `npm run
  entropy -- review --repository <id> [<commit>]` freezes a copy of the
  registered clone (`recordedRepositoryClone`, read in the order WO-223
  gives the moved-record reader) at the named commit, or at the clone's
  fetched base-branch head when none is named, exactly as the launchpad is
  frozen: a clone with no hard links and no checkout, detached at the
  commit, under the launchpad's scratch lane, with the dependency copy when
  the clone has one; the subject record's `repository` is the registration
  id, its hash covers it, and the receipt's subject names the repository,
  the commit and the frozen path. The pinned reviewer runs the same
  compiled program over that copy; the host revalidates the return; the
  receipt is filed and bound in the launchpad as today.
- **The refutation and the binding follow the subject.** `refute` freezes
  the same repository at the same commit for the blinded second worker; the
  filing's binding is the explicit-commit route (the named commit still
  resolves to the reviewed tree in the clone), the clone's refs and tracked
  status are witnessed before and after the episode and recorded, and the
  launchpad's own tracked status is recorded, not the subject.
- **Dispositions land in the launchpad's register and can target the
  workstream's orders.** `dispose … accept` appends the candidate under a
  heading that names the review, the repository and the commit, so the
  collector's row names the target and a planning pass allocates it with
  `--apply` to any order of the launchpad, the workstream's members
  included; proposal packets file under `docs/proposals/` as today.
- **A workstream is its member repositories.** `review --workstream WS-NNN` reads the distinct `repositoryId`s of the
  workstream document's `dotln-workstream` JSON block and dispatches the next
  member repository that has no filed review in the sequence (the launchpad
  itself when a member names `self`), returning as `review` does today; each
  receipt is filed by `entropy receipt` and carries the workstream id;
  `subject --workstream WS-NNN` names the next member to review, the pending
  dispatch or the receipt to consume, consuming before producing as today;
  each receipt's survivors are disposed in the pass (receipt 051).
- **The kit carries it.** The commands are kit files already; a kit fixture
  instance with a registered fixture target runs the subject and the review
  under the `fake` transport, and the review guide states the subjects.

orders.objective:
The source writer cannot damage the operator's repository,
and a writer's request reaches the operator. The writer's owned command
route and profile are removed by two independent, absence-tolerant
removals; a failed removal is a typed cleanup outcome naming the surviving
path; admission and after-tests refuse while any grant survives; settlement,
`WorkerInterrupted` and integrity are recorded before the cleanup's result
is judged; a restart removes the survivors and admits. Before the focused
after-tests the worktree is judged against the committed tree (a
`skip-worktree` or `assume-unchanged` entry, or a byte or mode differing
from the committed blob, refuses naming the path; nothing is restored), and
the verification worktree reads Git under the host's writer-resistant
argument set, so hidden modified, deleted and executable-bit files never
reach after-testing or publication and a planted configuration, replace ref
or commit graph cannot change what verification judges. The writer commits
on a detached worktree into a private object store, reading the shared
store through a read-only alternate with no write access to the shared
`objects`, `refs` or `logs`; after admission the host imports the
candidate's objects and only then creates the episode branch and updates
refs; the retained counterexample fails against the writer's access;
candidates still publish; a crash between import and ref update recovers
idempotently; concurrent `git gc` or `repack` neither loses data nor yields
an unjustified success. A writer that reports `status` other than
`completed`, or `requiresHuman`, ends its step `writer-requested-attention`
after the integrity and worktree checks, a rerun or restart keeps that end,
and the vertical records `NeedsHuman` with the request in its receipt. The
Codex writer's Git runs with rerere and automatic maintenance off, so its
`git commit -F` exits 0 under the `dotln-writer` grants while the shared Git
directory stays unwritable, requalified live at the installed Codex CLI on a
target with rerere enabled and packed refs, with denials read from the
host's own log. The Claude writer's launch environment carries the two
object-directory variables and the same two Git configuration pairs,
requalified live at the installed Claude CLI on a target with rerere
enabled: its commit lands in the private store, not the shared one, no
`rr-cache` and no maintenance write appears in the shared repository, and
the host imports and observes the commit. `dotln vertical` with a writer killed before commit exits 1
with a pending continuation, and a rerun completes the step with exactly one
commit. Ordinary recovery stays valid throughout.

With a replace ref, a commit graph or a hooks path planted by the writer,

Ordinary recovery of an unreceipted prior attempt passes under the new

The D033 counterexample, committed as a case, fails at the base and

A writer's commits land in the private object store and not in the

orders.title: WO-207 — Instance update control: an instance takes kit machinery with its build pinned or followed, keeps its own code at a manifest-excluded extension root that the kit's machinery loads through the SourceAdapter port and no update touches, rolls back its last update to the prior kit state, and takes a starter update only through an upgrade order its own planning pass cuts, gated by kit conformance and its own declared suites (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
An instance controls the kit updates it takes, from core and
inside the instance:

- **Its own code.** `dotln.config.json` may declare `extensions`: a root
  outside every kit tree (default `extensions/`) and adapters by kind
  (`source`, `effect`, `projection`). A vertical issue naming
  `source: "<id>"` has `prepare()` load that adapter, record
  `ExtensionLoaded { id, kind, path, sha256 }` and call its `fetchBundle`
  in place of `fetchIssueBundle`, with the bundle passing the same checks
  as the GitHub source's; `effect` and `projection` adapters are admitted
  and listed, never imported here. No export, manifest or update touches
  the root; the README states the review burden. The first consumer is a
  fixture adapter; the enterprise-tracker adapter is the work instance's.
- **Its build.** The kit manifest names its build (the compiled definition
  modules, their semantic hash and compiler version). An update takes
  `both` (today's), `machinery` (build modules kept at their pinned bytes,
  `build.pin` recorded, emit, check and `kit-verify` honoring it) or `build`
  (the build alone, then the re-emit), and refuses an incompatible pairing
  before any write; inside an instance, the upgrade order runs
  `build --pin` or `build --take` after its merge, as the channel the
  operator chose. WO-076's overlay composes over whichever build is pinned.
- **Its way back.** Each update logs what it did and keeps retained copies,
  refusing before any write when it cannot. `rollback` inside the instance,
  or `export --update <dir> --rollback` from core, returns the kit files
  and manifest to the logged state before the last update, reverses the
  reversible instance actions (the update's `build.pin` among them), lists
  the rest by id, logs itself and prints the re-emit, which the role that
  ran it runs next; it refuses, naming the path or row, after a later kit
  edit, when the update is not the latest, or when a prior file has no
  verified source.
- **Its way in.** An instance takes a starter update through the session-run
  route the client README records since WO-210: the incoming revision
  previewed from a detached worktree of that revision, the merge on an update
  branch, the re-emit and lineage index, one commit, the push and the update
  pull request the operator merges (the personal fork took its #1, #3, #8 and
  #16 this way). For the operator's instances the upgrade order a planning
  pass (dedicated, or part of one) cuts from the kit's template is that
  route's recorded form: it names the starter revision, the channel and each
  refused path's resolution, carries the route as its plan, runs the channel's
  `build` form after the merge and passes the gate below; the template's
  rollback form takes the way back the same way. A planning branch writes only
  `docs/` and root Markdown (WO-135), so the pass never applies kit files.
- **Its gate.** The consumer selection WO-213 decided (WO-213-D014: the six
  structural tasks and `kit-verify`, run fresh; carried kit suites stay
  explicit `--only` and `--machinery` diagnostics) plus the instance's own
  additions, the planner's proposal (assumption 8): suites it declares in
  `dotln.config.json` `suites` (name, command and sources), selected by
  changed sources, appended to that selection and run fresh, with each
  extension adapter naming the suite that covers it. Core's own gate is
  unchanged.
- **No step is the operator's by hand.** The operator gives the word (the
  starter revision, the channel, how each refused path resolves, a
  rollback), types the dispatch phrases and merges the pull request; a
  role runs every command and makes every commit (operator direction,
  2026-10-13; planning document §12.1).

The Repo Gardener equips the full six-piece 5S set. One link
group may hold several actives sharing linked supports: each keeps its own
WorkOrder seed, envelope and claims; a shared support's emissions,
precedence and commutativity apply per active; a non-commuting pair still
needs an explicit pipeline; a multi-active group beyond six links compiles
and carries a visible signal naming the decomposition question;
single-active programs normalize and hash exactly as before. An optional
`sets` collection names member active ids and bonuses, each with a piece
count and a list of emissions of existing kinds, as a support's `emissions`
is; absent normalizes to empty; the three editable views encode and decode
it; a bonus is armed when at least its piece count of members is equipped,
an armed bonus's emissions are lowered, and the compiled inspection lists
each bonus armed or dark with the arming count. Seiton, Seisō, Seiketsu,
Shitsuke and Safety join Seiri with canonical term, translation, kanji,
secondary RPG title, tags, WorkOrder seed, envelope and tooltip collections
following 05 (Shine makes cleaning double as inspection, Standardize turns a
recurring repair into a proposed test, rule, hook or script, Sustain is the
cadence, Safety is the parallel guard region), reusing the Entropy Reducer's
Shine and Standardize where semantics coincide and recording any
divergence; each compiles alone with a pinned tooltip, and all six compile
in one group. The set's five bonuses: at two pieces every Sort candidate
carries a proposed canonical home (evidence-schema); at three every cleanup
invokes an integrity check (verifier episode); at four a recurring repair
proposes a standardization (evidence field and work-order obligation); at
five the cycle schedules its own bounded reevaluation (a cadence in the
evaluable subset); at six, with Safety, a destructive change is legal only
with isolation, evidence, independent verification and explicit approval
(permission guard plus statechart gate), which the Gardener's base rank
refuses. Beside the frozen 13-step scenario, a full-set scenario equips all
six pieces against the deterministic fakes, live and replay produce
identical complete Decisions, and `--compiled-diff --loadout <id>` renders
each piece's tooltip and the set summary with each bonus armed or dark and
the three view hashes.

## Goal-aligned decisions

The Contributor's purpose comes from [the vision](00-vision.md): DotLn is a
local-first, model-agnostic compiler/runtime for human judgment. This personal
implementation aims to improve operator flow by moving recurring supervision,
coordination, recovery and verification into dependable machinery, while
preserving correctness, authority, evidence, privacy and recoverability.

The current [critical-path plan](../planning/critical-path-2026-09-08.md) targets
the always-on runtime, its first real external source change and an independently
verified source-to-deliverable loop.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

**Platform lens.** Four checks from the platforms lesson the operator
pointed at (Steve Yegge's 2011 account of the Amazon service mandate) apply
to any capability a plan or order lands: it arrives as an interface
something else consumes (a transport profile, a typed event, a projection, a
handoff packet), never only as a script or a session; it is externalizable
by construction (content-addressed inputs, declared contracts, no private
setting as the source of a guarantee); this repository and the operator's
own repository consume it before any export; and its result is usable by a
stranger to the session, so a receipt that needs reverse-engineering is an
accessibility failure [[vision-into-use pass](../planning/vision-into-use-2026-09-17.md)
§12, 2026-09-17]. The planning refuter's platform-first standard is
unchanged.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

The shared supports carry these duties and their compiled identity in both
harnesses. They are instruction-level judgment, not proof that an agent applied
every lens or a causal detector. The meter's five quantitative trap signals are
separate. General Naive Interventionism, NoOp and adaptive Tinkerer mechanics
retain their candidate scope; this bounded Contributor policy does not claim
their generalized implementations. The [WO-043 receipt](../evidence/WO-043/ideation-commands-and-usage.md)
records this promotion and its limits.
